items.title: Aston Villa latest: Emery explains Garnacho omission vs Coventry
Liverpool face Chelsea as Carabao Cup fourth-round draw confirmed
items.description: Liverpool will host Chelsea in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup, while Premier League champions Arsenal have drawn the lowest-ranked side left in the competition, Fleetwood Town.

items.title: Everton strike late to beat much-changed Wolves in Carabao Cup
items.description: Substitute Charly Alcaraz hit a late winner to give Everton a 1-0 home win over much-changed Wolves in the third round of the Carabao Cup.

items.title: Brighton complete SHOCK comeback to beat Man Utd
items.description: Highlights from the third round of the Carabao Cup match between Manchester United and Brighton.

items.title: De la Fuente extends Spain contract to 2032
items.description: World Cup-winning head coach Luis de la Fuente agrees a contract extension with Spain until 2032.

items.title: League Two Fleetwood host Arsenal in EFL Cup
items.description: League Two side Fleetwood Town will host Premier League champions Arsenal in the fourth round of the EFL Cup.

items.title: Man Utd collapse from 2-0 up to exit Carabao Cup to Brighton
items.description: Manchester United hit a new low under Michael Carrick as they threw away a two-goal lead to lose 3-2 to Brighton - and exit the Carabao Cup at the first hurdle for a second straight year.

items.title: Abraham double helps Villa cruise past Coventry into fourth round
items.description: Tammy Abraham scored twice as Aston Villa won 3-1 at Coventry City to book their place in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup.

items.title: Horror own goal sees Fleetwood shock Sheff Utd and book Arsenal tie
items.description: Rhys Norrington-Davies' horror own goal sent Fleetwood into the last 16 of the Carabao Cup for the first time as the League Two side stunned Championship Sheffield United 1-0 at Highbury.

items.title: Painful endgame for Gray as stale Hibs slump
items.description: A club hero, David Gray ends his time as Hibs head coach not to the sound of euphoria from fans, but to the sound of a support collectively exhaling in relief, writes Tom English.
